items.claim: The front seam of this span (a first-person voice change into the servant's report) is well warranted, but the row's ground for declining to cut web:Isa.50.10 away from that report treats tier-1 addressee-shift evidence inconsistently with how this same cluster applies that category elsewhere, which weakens the argued-from-tier-1-seams basis the servant_song unit_type requires.
items.evidence: web:Isa.50.10 opens with a second-person-plural direct-address interrogative turning to a new addressee, מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֔ה שֹׁמֵ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל עַבְדּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֣ךְ חֲשֵׁכִ֗ים וְאֵ֥ין נֹ֨גַהּ֙ ל֔וֹ יִבְטַח֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וְיִשָּׁעֵ֖ן בֵּאלֹהָֽיו (oshb:Isa.50.10, tier: byte) -- “Who among you fears Yahweh, who obeys the voice of his servant...” (web:Isa.50.10) -- which is the same class of explicit addressee shift this cluster treats as tier-1-sufficient on its own everywhere else in its own span: the fresh imperative-plus-addressee turn at web:Isa.51.1, שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם (oshb:Isa.51.1, tier: byte), at web:Isa.51.4, הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ (oshb:Isa.51.4, tier: byte), and at web:Isa.51.7, שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל תֵּחָֽתּוּ (oshb:Isa.51.7, tier: byte), is cut into three separate rows on fresh-imperative-plus-addressee grounds alone, with no massa, hoy, or messenger-formula present at any of the three onsets; and the addressee turn at web:Isa.51.21, לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי נָ֥א זֹ֖את עֲנִיָּ֑ה וּשְׁכֻרַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א מִיָּֽיִן (oshb:Isa.51.21, tier: byte) -- “Therefore hear this, you afflicted one...” (web:Isa.51.21) -- is treated as tier-1 even though it is joined to what precedes by a logical connective. Declining tier-1 status to web:Isa.50.10's addressee turn on the stated ground that no massa/hoy/messenger-formula opens there narrows the tier-1 category to those three formula-types alone and omits the addressee-shift category the cluster relies on at web:Isa.51.1/51.4/51.7/51.21. Parashah-paragraph continuity across web:Isa.50.4-Isa.50.11 is real (no interior mark sits between the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.50.3 and the PE at oshb:Isa.50.11) but is tier-3 corroboration only and cannot on its own repair that gap. The preceding divine speech itself opens with its own explicit frame, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣י זֶ֠ה סֵ֣פֶר כְּרִית֤וּת אִמְּכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שִׁלַּחְתִּ֔יהָ א֚וֹ מִ֣י מִנּוֹשַׁ֔י אֲשֶׁר מָכַ֥רְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם ל֑וֹ הֵ֤ן בַּעֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֔ם וּבְפִשְׁעֵיכֶ֖ם שֻׁלְּחָ֥ה אִמְּכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.50.1, tier: byte, “Thus says Yahweh”), confirming the first-person voice beginning at web:Isa.50.4 is a genuine new speaker distinct from that frame -- the front seam is not in question, only the coda's attachment.

items.claim: The span is bounded by a genuine tier-1 imperative-plus-addressee onset at its front and closes on its own comfort formula immediately before a differently-shaped fresh imperative opens the next unit, and its unit_type and rejected alternative are both accurately argued.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.1 opens with its own fresh vocative address, שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם (oshb:Isa.51.1, tier: byte), distinct in wording from the addressee turns that open both the following members of the series (web:Isa.51.4, web:Isa.51.7); the span's content -- the rock/quarry figure, the Abraham-and-Sarah appeal, and the Eden-like comfort of Zion at web:Isa.51.3 -- coheres as promise/comfort material matching the salvation_oracle default for this half of the book, and holding the whole three-member series as one span is a genuine, non-strawman rival rather than the strongest read, since each member reopens with its own fresh imperative form and closes on its own formula.

items.claim: The span's front boundary correctly turns on a distinct imperative verb form addressed to a fresh audience, and the row accurately names the form-class contrast with the preceding member of the series rather than asserting an unsupported recurrence.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.4 opens with הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ (oshb:Isa.51.4, tier: byte), a Hiphil-pattern imperative pair addressed to “my people... my nation,” verifiably distinct in shape from web:Isa.51.1's שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם (oshb:Isa.51.1, tier: byte); this is a legitimate tier-1 addressee-plus-form seam, and the disclosed rival -- reading the span as a bare continuation of the rock-and-quarry appeal -- is the genuine strongest alternative, correctly set aside on the same verb-shape-change ground.

items.claim: The span's boundaries are correctly argued from a third fresh imperative-plus-addressee onset closing the series, and the claimed recurrence of the first member's verb shape at this onset is byte-accurate.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.7 opens with שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל תֵּחָֽתּוּ (oshb:Isa.51.7, tier: byte), the same imperative shape used at web:Isa.51.1's שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם (oshb:Isa.51.1, tier: byte) but addressed to a distinct epithet (“you who know righteousness”) marking a fresh onset rather than a resumption; the span closes at web:Isa.51.8 on its own moth-and-worm/everlasting-righteousness formula immediately before the differently addressed web:Isa.51.9 appeal, and folding the pair into the preceding span is a real, non-strawman rival correctly set aside on the fresh-addressee ground.

items.claim: The span opens on a genuine tier-1 seam (a shift from human second-person address to a vocative petition addressed to Yahweh's arm) and its operative-category deviation from the salvation_oracle default to hymn_doxology is disclosed as required, with the referent question left open.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.9 opens with the doubled Qal imperative עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין (oshb:Isa.51.9, tier: byte), addressed to “arm of Yahweh” rather than to any human audience, a clear addressee-and-speaker-role change from the preceding “you who know righteousness” address of web:Isa.51.7-Isa.51.8; the span's content -- a community petition invoking Yahweh's past deeds (Rahab, the sea) rather than Yahweh's own promise-speech -- does not fit the salvation_oracle default cleanly, and the device_notes field names this deviation in one sentence as the closed vocabulary requires; the disclosed rejected alternative (splitting off web:Isa.51.11) correctly notes that verse carries no imperative, vocative, or messenger formula of its own.

items.claim: The span's front seam is a well-grounded speaker change from the community's petition to Yahweh's own first-person answer, correctly treated as tier-1, and the unit_type call and rejected alternative both track the bytes accurately.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.12 opens with the doubled self-identification אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם מִֽי אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמ֔וּת וּמִבֶּן אָדָ֖ם חָצִ֥יר יִנָּתֵֽן (oshb:Isa.51.12, tier: byte), a first-person divine answer distinct in speaker from the arm-directed petition of web:Isa.51.9-Isa.51.11; salvation_oracle correctly names this promise/comfort speech, and the disclosed rejected alternative -- holding web:Isa.51.9-Isa.51.16 as one unbroken petition-and-answer span -- is the genuine strongest rival, correctly set aside on the speaker-change ground rather than a strawman.

items.claim: The span's front seam (a second, differently-formed awake-imperative now addressed to Jerusalem) and its judgment_oracle deviation disclosure are both well-grounded, and the row correctly treats the addressee shift at web:Isa.51.21 as tier-1 despite the logical connective joining it to what precedes.
items.evidence: web:Isa.51.17 opens with the Hitpael doubled form הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י ק֚וּמִי יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁתִ֛ית מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת כּ֣וֹס חֲמָת֑וֹ אֶת קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֛ה שָׁתִ֖ית מָצִֽית (oshb:Isa.51.17, tier: byte), verifiably a different binyan from web:Isa.51.9's Qal doubled עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין (oshb:Isa.51.9, tier: byte), and is now addressed to Jerusalem rather than to Yahweh's arm; the span's own content (web:Isa.51.17-Isa.51.20) recounts wrath already suffered without itself announcing relief, and the device_notes field names judgment_oracle as an explicit closer-content-match deviation from the salvation_oracle default; the rejected alternative accurately identifies that a fresh imperative opens web:Isa.51.21 even though joined by a logical connective, and correctly treats that addressee shift as the tier-1 seam ending this span.
